metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index outdated <data-dir> --json`: a `vibe.lock` diffed against the index — one row per locked package, with upgrade candidates counted and the refusals named beside their rows. Read by scripts and agents (PROP-044 §6.5 — a CLI `--json` report is a format plain text; `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/outdated.rs` (`Envelope`, `Row`, `Status`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/outdated_report/`.
Always `"outdated"` for this report.
The lockfile path as the ask spelled it (`--lockfile`, default `vibe.lock`) — a `PathBuf` on the wire, verbatim: an absolute ask echoes absolute, a relative one relative.
How many rows carry `update-available` — the headline number of the report. `u32` in the writer.
One row per `[[package]]` of the lockfile, in the lockfile's own order. Required member: an empty lockfile writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
One locked package against the index: what is installed, what the newest usable stable is, and the verdict.
The locked package's kind — metadata per PROP-008 §2.3, read from the lockfile entry.
The locked package's group.
The locked package's bare name.
The version the lockfile pins.

The newest non-prerelease version this build can act on (`usable_latest_stable`), `null` when the index holds no such version for this package — a package absent from the index, or one whose every version is refused or a prerelease. The key is always present: the writer's `Option` carries no skip.
The verdict: `update-available` when `latest` outranks `installed`, `up-to-date` when it does not, `unknown` when there is no `latest` to compare against.

Versions of this name this build refuses to act on — the WHY beside the row, never a status change: `unknown` stays `unknown` (PROP-044 §4.5). Absent when there are none (the writer carries `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`).

The verdict on one locked package (closed vocabulary of three, kebab-case on the wire): `up-to-date` — the index's newest usable stable does not outrank the pin; `update-available` — it does; `unknown` — the index holds nothing comparable, and the row says why beside itself rather than guessing. Closed because every value already has a behaviour in the writer's `Status` enum — an unseen verdict has no safe reading.

One version this build refused to act on, and why — the row every `vibe-index` answering surface carries (`crates/vibe-index/src/index/quarantine.rs`, `Unavailable`). Local to this schema family: `formats/vocabularies.json` does not (yet) carry it, and each of the six report schemas that need it declare their own copy.
The refused version's group.
The refused version's bare package name.
The refused version.

The reader capabilities of `must_understand` this build lacks, in the record's own order. Required member: a refusal always writes its list, `[]` never occurring in practice today (a row exists exactly because the list is non-empty) but lawful on the wire — the writer has no skip here.
What a person or a script does about it — the fixed two-part text `recipe_for` builds (the explanation with the PROP-044 anchor, then the `fix:` surface).
